standard.title: Embedded clauses in complex sentences
standard.description: understand how embedded clauses can expand the variety of complex sentences to elaborate, extend and explain ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand that the structure of a complex sentence includes a main clause and at least one dependent clause (AC9E5LA05). They have not yet examined how embedded (relative) clauses are inserted within a main clause to expand noun groups, as distinct from adverbial dependent clauses that follow or precede the main clause.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand how embedded clauses expand noun groups within complex sentences and can use them to elaborate, extend and explain ideas.

nodes.label: What an embedded clause is
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify an embedded (relative) clause within a sentence and distinguish it from a trailing dependent clause.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the embedded clause in at least two provided example sentences (e.g. 'The town that was flooded suffered extensive damage'); explain how it is positioned inside the main clause rather than following it.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain embedded clauses across a range of provided sentences; distinguish between adverbial dependent clauses (e.g. 'Because it rained, the game was cancelled') and embedded clauses that expand noun groups within the main clause.
wider: Analyse a paragraph from a curriculum-area text (science, history) and identify where embedded clauses are used and what noun groups they expand
Compare the effect of an embedded clause vs a trailing clause in conveying the same information (e.g. 'The dog that bit me...' vs 'The dog bit me, and it...')
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot distinguish embedded from trailing clauses cannot attempt the Node 2 construction task — they will produce trailing dependent clauses and believe they have met the requirement.

response_modes.reason: Students who have only encountered trailing dependent clauses will classify all complex sentences as having the same structure. Encountering embedded clauses in multiple sentence contexts helps students build a more complete model of complex sentence variety.

success_criteria: Correctly identifies the embedded clause in at least two provided sentences
Explains how an embedded clause differs in position from a trailing dependent clause

nodes.label: Using embedded clauses to elaborate ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can construct complex sentences using embedded clauses to elaborate, extend and explain ideas, and explain why they have used an embedded clause in preference to other constructions.
nodes.minimum_width: Construct at least one sentence using an embedded clause to expand a noun group (e.g. 'Hamish studied the rock samples that he had collected on the excursion'); identify the embedded clause and what noun group it expands.
nodes.typical_width: Create and use complex sentences with embedded clauses in writing, selecting conjunctions that enable the clauses to elaborate, extend or explain; revise sentences to evaluate whether an embedded clause improves precision and variety.
wider: Experiment with stacking multiple clauses in a sentence and evaluate where embedded clauses create clarity vs. awkwardness
Edit a piece of own writing to introduce embedded clauses where they add precision, and reflect on the effect
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot produce accurate embedded clauses cannot deploy them in extended writing (Node 3 and AC9E6LY06) — the production skill must be established before the integration task is attempted.

response_modes.reason: Constructing embedded clauses accurately requires mechanical precision — students need practice producing them in varied sentences before they can deploy them fluently in extended writing. Fluency here enables transfer to AC9E6LY06.

success_criteria: Constructs a grammatically accurate sentence with an embedded clause
Identifies the embedded clause and names the noun group it expands

nodes.label: Embedded clauses in extended writing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can deploy embedded clauses in extended writing as part of a varied repertoire of complex sentence structures.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a short piece of extended writing (at least one paragraph) that uses at least one embedded clause accurately within a varied sentence structure.
nodes.typical_width: Write extended texts that use embedded clauses alongside other complex sentence structures; evaluate the variety and precision of complex sentences in own writing; edit to improve sentence variety where needed.
wider: Analyse a paragraph from a curriculum-area information report and identify all complex sentence types used, including any embedded clauses
Rewrite a provided paragraph using a greater variety of complex sentence structures, including embedded clauses, and evaluate the improvement

response_modes.reason: Deploying embedded clauses fluently in extended writing requires integrating identification knowledge (Node 1) with production skills (Node 2) in sustained compositional context — the transfer to extended writing is the integration challenge.

success_criteria: Produces at least one grammatically accurate embedded clause within a piece of extended writing
Demonstrates at least two different complex sentence structures in the same piece of writing
